learning_outcomes.text: Students have subject-specific basic knowledge for the confident mathematical handling of stochastic models for measured signals.
Students are qualified to solve signal processing problems with random signals and to apply practically relevant methods for parameter estimation in signal processing.

syllabus_topics: Probability distributions and probability density functions for processes
Moment functions of stochastic processes, definitions of first and second-order moment functions
Properties of covariance and correlation functions, stationarity, spectral power density, white noise
Binary decisions, Bayes decision, MAP test, Maximum Likelihood test, MiniMax test
Least squares estimation, Maximum Likelihood estimator
Estimation of the covariance function of a noise signal, spectral estimation, estimation of parameters of linear processes
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam.
